title: Sheet-Pan Lemon Herb Salmon with Asparagus
description: Tender salmon fillets and crisp-tender asparagus roasted together on one pan with garlic, lemon and fresh dill. Dinner is on the table in 25 minutes with almost no cleanup.

ingredients.name: salmon fillets
ingredients.note: 4 fillets, about 6 oz each, skin-on or skinless

steps: Heat the oven to 425°F and line a large rimmed baking sheet with parchment paper.
Toss the asparagus with 1 tablespoon olive oil, 1/2 teaspoon salt and a pinch of pepper. Spread it along the outer edges of the pan.

Pat the salmon dry and set it skin-side down in the center of the pan. Stir together the remaining 1 tablespoon olive oil, garlic, lemon juice, dill and parsley, then spoon it over the salmon. Season with the remaining salt and pepper and top each fillet with a lemon slice.
Roast for 12 to 15 minutes, until the salmon flakes easily with a fork and reads 130 to 135°F in the thickest part, and the asparagus is tender with lightly browned tips.
Rest for 2 minutes, then serve with any pan juices spooned over the top.

image.alt: Grilled salmon with asparagus and sauce

title: Crispy Tofu Quinoa Power Bowls
description: Golden oven-crisped tofu over fluffy quinoa with spinach, cucumber, cherry tomatoes and creamy avocado, finished with a bright lemon-garlic dressing. A satisfying plant-based bowl that also packs well for lunches.

ingredients.name: tamari
ingredients.note: or low-sodium soy sauce if gluten isn't a concern

steps: Heat the oven to 425°F and line a rimmed baking sheet with parchment paper. Press the tofu between towels under a heavy pan for 10 minutes to remove excess water, then cut it into 3/4-inch cubes.

In a large bowl, toss the tofu with the tamari and 1 tablespoon olive oil, then sprinkle with the cornstarch, garlic powder and smoked paprika and toss until evenly coated. Spread the cubes on the baking sheet in a single layer, without crowding.
Bake for 25 to 30 minutes, flipping halfway, until the tofu is golden and crisp on the edges.

Meanwhile, bring the quinoa and broth to a boil in a medium saucepan. Cover, reduce the heat to low and simmer for 15 minutes, until the liquid is absorbed. Let stand, covered, for 5 minutes, then fluff with a fork.
Whisk the remaining 3 tablespoons olive oil with the lemon juice, grated garlic, salt and pepper to make the dressing.

Divide the spinach and quinoa among 4 bowls. Top with the crispy tofu, cucumber, tomatoes and avocado, then drizzle with the dressing. For meal prep, store the bowls without avocado or dressing for up to 4 days.

image.alt: Bowl of quinoa with tofu and avocado

title: Turkey and Veggie Stuffed Peppers
description: Sweet bell peppers stuffed with lean ground turkey, brown rice, zucchini and tomatoes, then baked under a layer of melty mozzarella. A comforting, lighter family dinner that freezes well.
steps: Heat the oven to 375°F. Slice the tops off the peppers and remove the seeds and ribs. If they wobble, trim a thin sliver from the bottoms so they stand upright. Stand them in a 9x9-inch baking dish.
Heat the olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add the turkey and onion and cook for 6 to 7 minutes, breaking up the meat, until no pink remains.
Add the zucchini and garlic and cook for 3 minutes, until the zucchini softens. Stir in the diced tomatoes, rice, Italian seasoning, paprika, salt and pepper and simmer for 2 minutes.
Spoon the filling into the peppers, packing it gently and mounding it on top. Pour 1/4 cup water into the bottom of the dish.
Cover tightly with foil and bake for 30 minutes, until the peppers are tender when pierced with a knife.
Uncover, sprinkle with mozzarella and bake for another 8 to 10 minutes, until the cheese is melted and bubbly. Top with parsley and serve.

image.alt: a white plate topped with stuffed bell peppers

title: Mediterranean Chickpea Salad
description: Hearty chickpeas tossed with cucumber, cherry tomatoes, red onion, olives and feta in a zesty lemon-oregano vinaigrette. It's no-cook, packed with fiber and gets better as it sits.
steps: In a small bowl or jar, whisk or shake together the olive oil, red wine vinegar, lemon juice, garlic, oregano, salt and pepper.
Put the red onion in a large bowl, pour the dressing over it and let it sit for 5 minutes to mellow the onion's bite.
Pat the rinsed chickpeas dry with a towel, then add them to the bowl with the cucumber, tomatoes, olives and parsley. Toss to coat.
Fold in the feta, then taste and adjust with more salt, pepper or lemon juice.
Serve right away or refrigerate for up to 4 days. The flavor improves after 30 minutes in the fridge.

image.alt: A bowl of chana chaat with chickpeas, chopped tomatoes, onions, and cilantro

title: Shrimp and Broccoli Stir-Fry with Brown Rice
description: Plump shrimp and crisp-tender broccoli in a glossy garlic-ginger sauce, spooned over nutty brown rice. It's lighter and fresher than takeout.

ingredients.name: large shrimp
ingredients.note: peeled and deveined, thawed if frozen

steps: Cook the brown rice according to the package directions, usually simmered covered for 40 to 45 minutes. Keep warm.
While the rice cooks, whisk together the soy sauce, broth, honey, rice vinegar, cornstarch and sesame oil in a small bowl.

Heat 1/2 tablespoon vegetable oil in a large skillet or wok over high heat. Add the broccoli and 2 tablespoons water, cover and steam for 2 minutes. Uncover and stir-fry for 2 to 3 minutes, until bright green and crisp-tender. Transfer to a plate.

Add the remaining 1 tablespoon oil to the pan. Pat the shrimp dry and add them in a single layer. Cook for 1 to 2 minutes per side, until pink and just opaque. Add the garlic and ginger and stir for 30 seconds, until fragrant.
Return the broccoli to the pan. Stir the sauce again, pour it in and toss for 1 to 2 minutes, until it thickens and coats everything.
Serve over the brown rice, topped with green onions and red pepper flakes if you like.

image.alt: a plate of food with shrimp, rice, and vegetables

title: Black Bean Sweet Potato Tacos
description: Smoky roasted sweet potatoes and seasoned black beans tucked into warm corn tortillas with avocado, crunchy cabbage and a tangy lime yogurt crema. A colorful meatless taco night everyone will love.

ingredients.name: sweet potatoes
ingredients.note: about 2 medium, peeled and cut into 1/2-inch cubes

steps: Heat the oven to 425°F. On a rimmed baking sheet, toss the sweet potatoes with the olive oil, chili powder, cumin, paprika and 3/4 teaspoon salt. Spread in a single layer.
Roast for 15 minutes. Stir, scatter the black beans over the pan and roast for another 8 to 10 minutes, until the sweet potatoes are tender and caramelized at the edges.
Meanwhile, stir together the Greek yogurt, half the lime juice and the remaining 1/4 teaspoon salt to make the crema. Toss the cabbage with the rest of the lime juice.
Warm the tortillas in a dry skillet over medium-high heat for 30 seconds per side, or wrap them in a damp paper towel and microwave for 45 seconds.
Fill each tortilla with the sweet potato and black bean mixture, then top with cabbage, avocado, a drizzle of crema and cilantro. Serve with lime wedges.

image.alt: two tacos on a plate with a lime wedge

title: Greek Yogurt Berry Overnight Oats
description: Creamy, protein-boosted oats soaked overnight with Greek yogurt, chia and a touch of honey, then topped with juicy mixed berries. Breakfast is waiting in the fridge when you wake up.

ingredients.name: mixed berries
ingredients.note: fresh or frozen, such as strawberries, blueberries and raspberries

steps: In a large bowl, whisk together the almond milk, Greek yogurt, honey, vanilla and salt until smooth.
Stir in the oats and chia seeds until fully coated.
Divide the mixture among 4 jars or containers with lids, about 1 cup each. Top each with 1/2 cup berries. Frozen berries will thaw overnight.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 6 hours or overnight, up to 4 days.
In the morning, stir and add a splash of milk if it's too thick. Eat cold or microwave for 1 to 2 minutes.

image.alt: oats with cream and strawberries

title: Hearty Lentil Vegetable Soup
description: A thick, cozy pot of lentils simmered with carrots, celery, tomatoes and warm spices, with spinach stirred in at the end. Filling, freezer-friendly and very inexpensive.

ingredients.name: brown lentils
ingredients.note: dry, rinsed and picked over (green lentils also work)

steps: Heat the olive oil in a large Dutch oven or soup pot over medium heat. Add the onion, carrots and celery with a pinch of salt and cook for 7 to 8 minutes, stirring occasionally, until softened.
Add the garlic, tomato paste, cumin, paprika and thyme. Cook for 1 minute, stirring, until fragrant and the tomato paste darkens slightly.
Stir in the lentils, diced tomatoes, broth, salt and pepper. Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat to low, partially cover and simmer for 25 to 30 minutes, until the lentils are tender.
For a thicker soup, blend about 2 cups of it with an immersion blender, or in a blender and return it to the pot.
Stir in the spinach and cook for 1 to 2 minutes, until wilted. Turn off the heat and stir in the lemon juice.
Taste and adjust the seasoning before serving. Leftovers keep for 5 days in the fridge or 3 months in the freezer.

image.alt: a close up of a bowl of food on a table

title: Baked Cod with Roasted Cherry Tomatoes
description: Flaky white cod baked on a bed of blistered cherry tomatoes, garlic and capers that collapse into a quick pan sauce. It's light and bright, and ready in 30 minutes.

ingredients.name: cod fillets
ingredients.note: 4 fillets, about 6 oz each, thawed if frozen

steps: Heat the oven to 425°F. In a 9x13-inch baking dish, toss the cherry tomatoes, garlic, capers, red pepper flakes, oregano, 2 tablespoons olive oil and 1/2 teaspoon salt.
Roast the tomatoes for 10 minutes, until they start to soften and a few burst.
Meanwhile, pat the cod dry. Brush it with the remaining 1 tablespoon olive oil and season with the remaining 1/2 teaspoon salt, the pepper and the lemon zest.
Push the tomatoes to the sides and nestle the cod in the center of the dish, spooning a few tomatoes and some of the juices over the fish.
Bake for 10 to 12 minutes, until the cod is opaque and flakes easily with a fork, reaching 145°F inside.
Squeeze a lemon wedge over the dish, sprinkle with parsley and serve with the tomatoes and pan juices spooned over the fish.

image.alt: Cooked fish, rice, roasted brussels sprouts, tomatoes, and capers

title: Spinach and Feta Egg Muffins
description: Fluffy baked egg bites filled with spinach, red pepper, green onion and salty feta. Make a dozen on Sunday for grab-and-go, protein-packed breakfasts all week.

ingredients.name: kosher salt
ingredients.note: feta is salty, so go light

steps: Heat the oven to 350°F. Generously coat a 12-cup muffin tin with cooking spray, or use silicone liners.
Divide the spinach, bell pepper, green onions and feta evenly among the 12 cups.
In a large bowl or 4-cup measuring cup, whisk the eggs, milk, garlic powder, salt and pepper until completely smooth.
Pour the egg mixture over the vegetables, filling each cup about three-quarters full.
Bake for 18 to 22 minutes, until the centers are set and no longer jiggle and the tops are lightly golden.

Cool in the pan for 5 minutes, then run a thin knife around the edges to release them. Serve 3 per person. Refrigerate up to 5 days or freeze up to 2 months, and reheat for 30 to 45 seconds in the microwave.

image.alt: Small spinach quiches arranged in a row on a wooden serving tray

title: Black Bean and Rice Burrito Bowls
description: Cumin-spiced black beans and corn over fluffy lime rice, piled high with salsa, cheddar and crunchy lettuce. A filling Tex-Mex dinner that costs less than takeout chips and dip.
steps: Rinse the rice in a fine-mesh strainer. Combine with 2 cups water and 1/2 tsp kosher salt in a medium saucepan, bring to a boil, then cover, reduce heat to low and simmer 18 minutes. Remove from heat and let stand covered 5 minutes.

While the rice cooks, heat the olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add the onion and cook 5 minutes until softened, then add the garlic, chili powder and cumin and cook 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add the black beans, frozen corn and 1/4 cup water. Simmer 6-8 minutes, stirring and lightly mashing some of the beans, until the corn is hot and the mixture is saucy. Season with salt.
Fluff the rice with a fork and stir in the juice of 1 lime and half of the cilantro.
Divide the rice among 4 bowls and top with the bean and corn mixture, shredded lettuce, salsa, cheddar and a spoonful of sour cream.
Sprinkle with the remaining cilantro and serve with lime wedges. Leftover rice and beans keep 4 days in the fridge; store toppings separately.

image.alt: Burrito bowl with rice, beans and toppings

title: Pasta e Fagioli
description: The classic Italian pasta-and-bean soup: tender ditalini and creamy cannellini beans in a garlicky tomato broth, finished with Parmesan. Hearty, cheap and even better the next day.

ingredients.name: ditalini pasta
ingredients.note: about 1 1/4 cups; small shells also work

steps: Heat the olive oil in a large Dutch oven or soup pot over medium heat. Add the onion, carrots and celery with a pinch of salt and cook 8 minutes, stirring often, until softened.
Stir in the garlic, oregano and red pepper flakes and cook 1 minute until fragrant.

Add the diced tomatoes with their juices, the cannellini beans and the broth. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer 10 minutes. Mash about 1/2 cup of the beans against the side of the pot to thicken the soup.
Return to a boil, add the ditalini and cook uncovered 9-10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the pasta is tender.
Season with salt and pepper. If the soup gets too thick, add a splash of water or broth.
Ladle into bowls and top with grated Parmesan and a drizzle of olive oil. The pasta absorbs liquid as it sits, so thin leftovers with broth when reheating.

image.alt: a bowl of pasta soup with a spoon in it

title: Chicken Thigh and Potato Traybake
description: Crispy-skinned paprika chicken thighs roasted on one pan with golden potatoes, onions and green beans. Hands-off, high-protein and made with one of the cheapest cuts at the meat counter.
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F with a rack in the upper-middle position. Pat the chicken thighs very dry with paper towels.
Mix the smoked paprika, garlic powder, thyme, 1 1/2 tsp salt and the pepper in a small bowl.
On a large rimmed sheet pan, toss the potatoes, onion wedges and garlic with 2 tbsp olive oil and half of the spice mix. Spread in an even layer.
Rub the chicken with the remaining 1 tbsp oil and remaining spice mix. Nestle the thighs skin-side up among the potatoes, leaving space between pieces.

Roast 30 minutes. Toss the green beans with a drizzle of oil and 1/2 tsp salt, scatter them around the chicken and roast 12-15 minutes more, until the skin is crisp, the potatoes are golden and the chicken reads 175°F at the thickest part.
Rest 5 minutes, squeeze lemon wedges over everything and serve straight from the pan, spooning the pan juices over the potatoes.

image.alt: Roasted chicken and potatoes served on a bed of greens

title: Veggie Egg Fried Rice
description: Better-than-takeout fried rice with fluffy scrambled eggs, peas, carrots and scallions, ready in 25 minutes. The best use for leftover rice and a bag of frozen vegetables.

ingredients.name: green onions
ingredients.note: thinly sliced, whites and greens separated

steps: Break up any clumps in the cold rice with your hands. Beat the eggs with a pinch of salt in a small bowl.
Heat 1 tbsp vegetable oil in a large nonstick skillet or wok over medium-high heat. Add the eggs and scramble 1-2 minutes until just set but still soft. Transfer to a plate.
Add the remaining 2 tbsp oil to the pan. Add the frozen peas and carrots and the green onion whites and stir-fry 3 minutes until hot. Add the garlic and cook 30 seconds.
Add the rice, spread it across the pan and let it sit 1 minute to toast, then stir-fry 4-5 minutes over high heat until every grain is hot and lightly crisped.
Drizzle the soy sauce around the edge of the pan, add the pepper and toss well. Fold the eggs back in, breaking them into bite-size pieces.
Turn off the heat, stir in the sesame oil and green onion greens, taste for more soy sauce and serve right away.

image.alt: A mound of fried rice with peas and carrots on a white square plate

title: Lentil Sloppy Joes
description: All the sweet-tangy, saucy comfort of classic sloppy joes made with hearty brown lentils instead of beef. Kids love them, and the filling freezes beautifully.
steps: Combine the lentils and 3 cups water in a medium saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer uncovered 20-25 minutes until tender but not mushy. Drain any excess water.

Meanwhile, heat the olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add the onion and bell pepper with a pinch of salt and cook 7-8 minutes until soft. Add the garlic and chili powder and cook 1 minute.
Stir in the tomato paste and cook 1 minute, then add the tomato sauce, ketchup, brown sugar, mustard and soy sauce.
Add the cooked lentils, bring to a simmer and cook 8-10 minutes, stirring often, until thick and saucy. Mash some of the lentils with a spoon for a meatier texture. Season with salt.
Toast the buns cut-side down in a dry skillet or under the broiler for 1-2 minutes.
Spoon a generous 3/4 cup of the lentil mixture onto each bun and serve. Cooled filling freezes up to 3 months.

image.alt: Sloppy joe sandwich on a black round plate

title: Baked Stuffed Manicotti
description: Tender pasta tubes stuffed with a creamy ricotta and spinach filling, baked in marinara under a golden layer of melted mozzarella. An Italian-restaurant favorite made affordable with frozen spinach and jarred sauce.

ingredients.name: kosher salt
ingredients.note: plus more for the pasta water

steps: Heat the oven to 375°F. Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil and cook the manicotti shells 2 minutes less than the package directions, about 6 minutes, so they stay firm enough to fill. Drain and lay flat on an oiled sheet pan to cool.
In a bowl, mix the ricotta, squeezed spinach, egg, 1/2 cup of the mozzarella, 1/4 cup of the Parmesan, garlic powder, Italian seasoning, salt and pepper until evenly combined.
Spoon the filling into a gallon zip-top bag, snip off one corner and pipe it into each shell from both ends until full.
Spread 1 cup of the marinara over the bottom of a 9x13-inch baking dish. Arrange the stuffed shells in a single layer and pour the remaining sauce over them, covering the pasta completely.
Sprinkle with the remaining 1 cup mozzarella and 1/4 cup Parmesan. Cover tightly with foil and bake 30 minutes, then uncover and bake 10-15 minutes more until bubbling and golden in spots.
Rest 10 minutes before serving, allowing 3-4 manicotti per person. To freeze, assemble without baking, wrap well and freeze up to 3 months; thaw overnight before baking.

image.alt: Baked stuffed manicotti casserole in the oven

title: Chana Masala
description: The North Indian classic: chickpeas simmered in a tangy, warmly spiced onion-tomato gravy with ginger, garlic and garam masala. Scooped up with warm store-bought naan, it's a deeply satisfying dinner from mostly pantry staples.
steps: Heat the oil in a large deep skillet or Dutch oven over medium heat. Add the onion and cook 10-12 minutes, stirring often, until deep golden brown; this builds the base flavor of the gravy.
Add the garlic, ginger and jalapeno and cook 1 minute. Stir in the coriander, cumin, 1 tsp of the garam masala, turmeric and cayenne and cook 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add the crushed tomatoes and salt and cook 5 minutes, stirring, until the sauce thickens and the oil starts to separate at the edges.
Stir in the chickpeas and water. Bring to a simmer, cover partially and cook 12-15 minutes. Mash about a quarter of the chickpeas against the pan to thicken the gravy.
Stir in the remaining 1 tsp garam masala and the lemon juice. Taste and adjust salt and heat.
Warm the naan in a 350°F oven or a dry skillet for 1-2 minutes per side. Serve the chana masala topped with cilantro, with the naan on the side. Leftovers keep 4 days refrigerated.

image.alt: A bowl of chana masala garnished with cilantro and ginger beside fried bhatura bread

title: Sausage, Peppers and Onions
description: Browned Italian sausages tucked into a skillet of sweet, jammy bell peppers and onions, piled into toasted hoagie rolls. Street-fair flavor on a weeknight budget.
steps: Heat the olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add the sausages and brown on all sides, turning occasionally, 8-10 minutes. Transfer to a cutting board.
Add the peppers, onions and salt to the drippings in the pan. Cook 10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until softened and starting to caramelize.
Stir in the garlic, oregano and red pepper flakes and cook 1 minute.
Slice the sausages into thick coins or leave whole, return them to the pan with 1/4 cup water, cover and cook 5-6 minutes until the sausages reach 160°F and the vegetables are jammy.
Season with black pepper. Toast the hoagie rolls cut-side down in a dry skillet or under the broiler for 1-2 minutes.
Pile the sausage, peppers and onions into the rolls and serve. Skip the rolls and serve over rice or pasta if you prefer.

image.alt: Sausage cooked with onions and green pepper

title: Banana Oat Pancakes
description: Fluffy, naturally sweet pancakes blended from ripe bananas, rolled oats and eggs, no flour needed. A wholesome weekend breakfast that uses up spotty bananas.
steps: Add the bananas, oats, eggs, milk, baking powder, cinnamon, vanilla and salt to a blender. Blend on high about 45 seconds until completely smooth.
Let the batter rest 5 minutes so the oats absorb liquid and it thickens slightly.
Heat a large nonstick skillet or griddle over medium-low heat and brush lightly with butter.
Pour 1/4 cup batter per pancake. Cook 2-3 minutes until bubbles form on top and the edges look set, then flip and cook 1-2 minutes more until golden.
Repeat with the remaining batter, adding butter to the pan as needed. Keep finished pancakes warm in a 200°F oven.
Serve with a drizzle of maple syrup and sliced banana or berries if you have them.

image.alt: baked pancake with blueberry and slice of banan

title: Tuna Melt Sandwiches
description: Tangy, crunchy tuna salad and sharp cheddar griddled between buttery slices of bread until golden and melty. A diner classic made from pantry cans in 20 minutes.
steps: In a bowl, flake the drained tuna with a fork and stir in the mayonnaise, celery, relish, Dijon, lemon juice and a few grinds of black pepper.
Thinly butter one side of each bread slice. Place 4 slices butter-side down on a cutting board.
Divide the tuna salad among the 4 slices, spreading to the edges, then top each with a slice of cheddar and the remaining bread, butter-side up.

Heat a large nonstick skillet or griddle over medium-low heat. Cook the sandwiches 3-4 minutes per side, pressing gently with a spatula, until deep golden and the cheese is melted. Cover the pan for the last minute to help the cheese melt.
Let rest 1 minute, slice in half diagonally and serve hot with pickles or a green salad.

image.alt: A grilled tuna melt sandwich with char marks beside a small bowl of greens

title: Zucchini Noodle Turkey Bolognese
description: A slow-simmered, herby turkey and tomato meat sauce spooned over tender zucchini noodles. All the comfort of spaghetti night at a fraction of the calories.

ingredients.name: zucchini
ingredients.note: spiralized, or two 10-oz packages zucchini noodles

steps: Heat the olive oil in a large deep skillet or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Add the ground turkey and cook, breaking it into small crumbles, until no longer pink, 6 to 7 minutes.
Add the onion, carrot and celery with a pinch of salt. Cook, stirring, until softened, about 5 minutes. Stir in the garlic and cook 30 seconds until fragrant.
Stir in the tomato paste and cook 1 minute, then add the crushed tomatoes, Italian seasoning and red pepper flakes. Bring to a simmer.
Reduce heat to medium-low and simmer uncovered, stirring occasionally, until thick and rich, 15 to 20 minutes. Season with salt and pepper.

Meanwhile, heat a separate nonstick skillet over medium-high heat. Add the zucchini noodles with a pinch of salt and toss just until warmed and barely tender, 2 to 3 minutes. Drain off any liquid so the sauce doesn't get watery.
Divide the zucchini noodles among 4 bowls, top with the bolognese, and finish with parmesan and torn basil.

image.alt: Zucchini noodles with meat sauce and a sauce jar

title: Chicken Cauliflower Fried Rice
description: Takeout-style fried rice made with riced cauliflower, juicy chicken, scrambled egg and peas and carrots. Ready in 25 minutes and packed with protein.
steps: Heat the vegetable oil in a large nonstick skillet or wok over medium-high heat. Add the chicken, season lightly with salt, and cook until golden and cooked through (165°F), 6 to 7 minutes. Transfer to a plate.
Pour the beaten eggs into the empty skillet and scramble just until set, about 1 minute. Add to the plate with the chicken.
Add the peas and carrots, garlic and ginger to the skillet and stir-fry 1 to 2 minutes until fragrant.
Add the frozen riced cauliflower straight from the bag. Spread it out and cook, stirring only every minute or so, until hot and any liquid has cooked off, 5 to 6 minutes.
Return the chicken and eggs to the pan. Add the soy sauce and sesame oil and toss over high heat for 1 minute so the edges toast slightly.
Stir in most of the green onions, taste for salt, and serve topped with the remaining green onions.

image.alt: Fried rice with chicken and vegetables on a plate

title: Asian Chicken Lettuce Wraps
description: Savory hoisin-ginger ground chicken with crunchy water chestnuts and peppers, spooned into cool butter lettuce cups. A fun, hands-on dinner the whole family loves.
steps: Whisk the hoisin, soy sauce, rice vinegar, sriracha and sesame oil in a small bowl; set aside.

Heat the vegetable oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add the ground chicken and cook, breaking it into small crumbles, until browned and cooked through, 6 to 7 minutes. Drain any excess fat.
Add the bell pepper, garlic and ginger and cook, stirring, until the pepper is crisp-tender, about 2 minutes.
Stir in the water chestnuts and the sauce. Cook 1 to 2 minutes until the sauce coats the chicken and looks glossy. Remove from heat and stir in most of the green onions.
Spoon the filling into lettuce leaves and top with shredded carrots and the remaining green onions. Serve right away, about 3 wraps per person.

image.alt: a lettuce wrap filled with meat and vegetables

title: Skillet Shrimp Fajitas
description: Smoky chili-lime shrimp seared with sweet bell peppers and red onion in a sizzling cast-iron skillet, then piled into warm corn tortillas with avocado and a Greek yogurt crema.

ingredients.name: large shrimp
ingredients.note: peeled and deveined, thawed if frozen

steps: Stir together the chili powder, cumin, smoked paprika, garlic powder and salt. Pat the shrimp dry and toss with half the spice mix and the juice of 1 lime.

Heat 1 tbsp olive oil in a 12-inch cast-iron skillet over medium-high heat until shimmering. Add the peppers and onion with the remaining spice mix and cook, stirring occasionally, until charred in spots and crisp-tender, 6 to 7 minutes. Transfer to a plate.
Add the remaining 1 tbsp olive oil to the skillet. Add the shrimp in a single layer and sear 1.5 to 2 minutes per side until pink and opaque.
Return the peppers and onions to the skillet and toss with the shrimp for 30 seconds so everything sizzles together. Squeeze a lime wedge over the top.

Meanwhile, stir a squeeze of lime into the Greek yogurt with a pinch of salt. Warm the tortillas in a dry skillet over medium heat, about 30 seconds per side, or wrapped in a damp towel in the microwave for 45 seconds.
Bring the skillet to the table and fill the tortillas with shrimp and vegetables. Top with avocado, lime crema and cilantro.

image.alt: Sizzling shrimp and vegetables served in a cast iron skillet

title: Lean Turkey Chili
description: A thick, hearty chili loaded with lean turkey, two kinds of beans and smoky spices. Big on protein and fiber, and even better the next day.
steps: Heat the olive oil in a large Dutch oven or heavy pot over medium-high heat. Add the turkey and cook, breaking it up, until browned, 6 to 7 minutes.
Add the onion, bell pepper and jalapeno and cook until softened, about 5 minutes. Stir in the garlic, chili powder, cumin, smoked paprika and oregano and cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the crushed tomatoes, kidney beans, black beans and broth. Stir well, scraping up any browned bits, and bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low, partially cover, and simmer, stirring occasionally, until thick, 25 to 30 minutes. Season with salt.
Ladle into bowls and top each with cheddar, a spoonful of Greek yogurt and green onions. Leftovers keep 4 days in the fridge or 3 months in the freezer.

image.alt: A bowl of chili with kidney beans, melted cheese, sour cream, and green onions

title: Veggie Egg White Scramble
description: Fluffy egg whites and a few whole eggs scrambled with crispy golden potatoes, spinach, peppers and feta. A filling, high-protein breakfast for about 340 calories.
steps: Place the diced potatoes in a microwave-safe bowl with 2 tbsp water, cover, and microwave on high 4 minutes until just tender. Drain well.

Heat the olive oil in a large nonstick skillet over medium-high heat. Add the potatoes in an even layer with a pinch of salt and cook, turning occasionally, until golden and crisp at the edges, 7 to 8 minutes.
Add the onion and bell pepper and cook 3 minutes until softened. Add the spinach and stir until just wilted, about 1 minute.
Whisk the egg whites, whole eggs, garlic powder, 1/2 tsp salt and a few grinds of pepper. Reduce heat to medium-low and pour over the vegetables.
Let the eggs set for 20 seconds, then gently push them across the pan with a spatula, forming soft curds. Keep folding until just set but still glossy, 3 to 4 minutes.
Sprinkle with feta and serve right away with salsa.

image.alt: Steaming scrambled eggs with potatoes and spinach on a grey plate

title: Classic Vegetable Minestrone
description: A cozy Italian soup brimming with vegetables, cannellini beans and little pasta in a tomato-herb broth. Light, filling and freezer-friendly.
steps: Heat the olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the onion, carrots and celery with a pinch of salt and cook, stirring occasionally, until softened, 6 to 8 minutes.
Stir in the garlic, zucchini, green beans and Italian seasoning and cook 2 minutes.
Add the diced tomatoes, broth and bay leaf. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer 10 minutes until the vegetables are nearly tender.
Stir in the cannellini beans and pasta and simmer, stirring occasionally, until the pasta is al dente, 9 to 11 minutes.
Add the peas and spinach and cook 1 to 2 minutes until the peas are hot and the spinach wilts. Remove the bay leaf and season with salt and pepper.
Ladle into bowls and top with parmesan. If making ahead, the pasta will absorb broth; thin with a splash of water or broth when reheating.

image.alt: two bowls of soup with peas, carrots and broccoli

title: Grilled Chicken Cobb Salad
description: Crisp romaine topped with sliced grilled chicken, hard-boiled egg, bacon, avocado, tomatoes and blue cheese, tossed with a tangy Dijon vinaigrette.
steps: Place the eggs in a saucepan, cover with cold water by 1 inch, and bring to a boil. Cover, remove from heat and let stand 10 minutes, then transfer to ice water. Peel and quarter.
Meanwhile, pound the chicken to an even 3/4-inch thickness. Rub with 1 tsp olive oil, garlic powder, smoked paprika, 1/2 tsp salt and pepper.
Heat a grill pan or outdoor grill to medium-high (about 425°F). Grill the chicken 5 to 6 minutes per side until it reaches 165°F. Rest 5 minutes, then slice.
Cook the bacon in a skillet over medium heat until crisp, 6 to 8 minutes. Drain on paper towels and crumble.
Whisk the remaining 2 tbsp olive oil, red wine vinegar, Dijon, a pinch of salt and pepper in a small jar or bowl.
Divide the romaine among 4 plates. Arrange rows of chicken, egg, bacon, tomatoes, avocado, red onion and blue cheese on top, and drizzle with the vinaigrette just before serving.

image.alt: A colorful salad with chicken and egg

title: Greek Turkey Meatballs with Tzatziki
description: Juicy oregano-and-feta turkey meatballs baked until golden, served with turmeric rice, a crisp cucumber-tomato salad and cool garlicky tzatziki.

ingredients.name: red onion
ingredients.note: half finely minced for meatballs, half thinly sliced for salad

ingredients.name: olive oil
ingredients.note: 1 tsp for the pan, 1 tbsp for the salad

ingredients.name: English cucumber
ingredients.note: half grated for tzatziki, half diced for salad

steps: Heat oven to 425°F. Line a rimmed baking sheet with parchment and brush with 1 tsp olive oil.

In a large bowl, combine the turkey, panko, egg, feta, minced red onion, two-thirds of the garlic, oregano, parsley, 3/4 tsp salt and 1/4 tsp pepper. Mix gently with your hands just until combined, then roll into 16 meatballs (about 1.5 inches) and set on the sheet.
Bake 18 to 20 minutes, until browned and cooked through (165°F).

Meanwhile, rinse the rice, then combine it in a saucepan with the broth, turmeric and a pinch of salt. Bring to a boil, cover, reduce heat to low and simmer 15 minutes. Remove from heat and let stand covered 5 minutes, then fluff.
For the tzatziki, squeeze the grated cucumber in a towel to remove excess water, then stir it into the Greek yogurt with the remaining garlic, dill, 1 tbsp lemon juice and a pinch of salt.
Toss the diced cucumber, cherry tomatoes, sliced red onion and romaine with 1 tbsp olive oil, the remaining lemon juice, salt and pepper.
Divide the rice, salad and meatballs among 4 plates and spoon tzatziki over the meatballs.

image.alt: Savory meatballs served with yellow rice, salad, and white sauce

title: Pan-Seared Cod with Ginger-Garlic Cream and Bok Choy
description: Golden pan-seared cod over sauteed mushrooms and baby bok choy, finished with a light, silky ginger-garlic cream sauce brightened with lime.

ingredients.name: cod fillets
ingredients.note: four 6-oz fillets, thawed if frozen; sea bass also works

steps: Pat the cod very dry and season both sides with salt and pepper.

Heat the olive oil in a large nonstick or cast-iron skillet over medium-high heat. Add the cod and sear without moving until a golden crust forms, 3 to 4 minutes. Flip and cook 2 to 3 minutes more until it flakes easily (145°F). Transfer to a plate.

In the same skillet, add the mushrooms with a pinch of salt and cook until browned, 4 minutes. Add the bok choy and sesame oil, toss, then add 2 tbsp water, cover and steam until crisp-tender, 2 to 3 minutes. Divide among plates.
Reduce heat to medium and melt the butter in the skillet. Add the garlic and ginger and cook 30 seconds until fragrant.
Pour in the broth and simmer 2 minutes to reduce slightly, then stir in the half-and-half and simmer 1 to 2 minutes until lightly thickened. Stir in 1 tbsp lime juice and season with salt.
Warm the brown rice according to the package. Set the cod on the vegetables, spoon the ginger-garlic cream over the top, and serve with rice, green onions and the remaining lime juice.

image.alt: Fish dish with creamy sauce and bok choy

title: Steak and Rice Burrito Bowls
description: Chili-lime seared sirloin over cilantro-lime rice with black beans, charred corn, cheese and fresh salsa. A restaurant-style burrito bowl you can meal prep for the week.
steps: Cook the rice: bring 2 cups water, the rice and 1/2 tsp kosher salt to a boil in a saucepan, cover, reduce heat to low and simmer 18 minutes. Rest 5 minutes off heat, then fluff with the juice of 1 lime and half the cilantro.
Meanwhile, pat the steak dry. Mix chili powder, cumin, garlic powder, 1 tsp kosher salt and 1/2 tsp black pepper; rub all over the steak with 1 tbsp olive oil.
Heat a large cast-iron or heavy skillet over medium-high heat until very hot. Sear the steak 4 to 5 minutes per side for medium-rare (130°F internal). Transfer to a cutting board and rest 5 minutes.

Wipe out the skillet, add the remaining 1 tbsp olive oil and the frozen corn. Cook over high heat 4 to 5 minutes, stirring rarely, until lightly charred. Push to one side, add the black beans and warm 2 minutes; season with salt.
Slice the steak thinly against the grain and squeeze the remaining lime over it.
Divide rice among 4 bowls and top with steak, beans, corn, cheese, pico de gallo and avocado. Finish with the remaining cilantro.

image.alt: Steak bowl, salad, and a refreshing drink on a table

title: Chicken Pasta with Mushrooms and Cherry Tomatoes
description: Juicy seared chicken breast sliced over fettuccine tossed in a silky garlic-Parmesan sauce with browned mushrooms and blistered cherry tomatoes.
steps: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Cook the fettuccine until al dente, about 10 minutes. Reserve 1/2 cup pasta water, then drain.

Meanwhile, pound the chicken to an even 3/4-inch thickness and season with Italian seasoning, 3/4 tsp kosher salt and 1/2 tsp black pepper. Heat 1 tbsp olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat and cook the chicken 5 to 6 minutes per side until golden and 165°F inside. Transfer to a board and rest 5 minutes.

Add the remaining 1 tbsp oil and the mushrooms to the same skillet. Cook 5 to 6 minutes, stirring occasionally, until browned. Add the cherry tomatoes and cook 2 to 3 minutes until they start to blister and soften.
Reduce heat to medium, add the butter and garlic and stir 1 minute until fragrant. Pour in the chicken broth, scraping up the browned bits, and simmer 3 minutes to reduce slightly.
Stir in the half-and-half and Parmesan until smooth. Add the drained fettuccine and toss 1 to 2 minutes, adding pasta water as needed for a silky sauce. Season with salt and pepper.
Slice the chicken and arrange over the pasta. Garnish with parsley and extra Parmesan.

image.alt: Sliced grilled chicken breast over pasta with vegetables

title: Teriyaki Salmon Rice Bowls
description: Broiled salmon brushed with a quick homemade honey-ginger teriyaki, served over rice with edamame, crunchy cucumber and carrots.
steps: Rinse the rice and cook with 2 1/4 cups water: bring to a boil, cover, reduce to low and simmer 15 minutes, then rest 10 minutes off heat.

Make the teriyaki: in a small saucepan whisk soy sauce, honey, rice vinegar, ginger, garlic, cornstarch and 3 tbsp water. Simmer over medium heat 2 to 3 minutes, stirring, until thickened. Set aside half for serving.
Heat the broiler to high with a rack 6 inches from the heat. Line a sheet pan with foil, add the salmon and brush with half the remaining teriyaki.
Broil 7 to 9 minutes, brushing with the rest of the glaze halfway through, until the salmon flakes easily and reaches 135 to 140°F in the thickest part.
Meanwhile, cook the edamame in boiling water or the microwave per package directions, about 4 minutes; drain.
Divide rice among 4 bowls. Top with salmon, edamame, cucumber and carrots. Drizzle with the reserved teriyaki and sprinkle with green onions and sesame seeds.

image.alt: a white plate topped with rice and a piece of salmon

title: Ground Turkey Sweet Potato Hash
description: Crispy diced sweet potatoes, smoky seasoned ground turkey, peppers and spinach in one skillet, finished with eggs baked right on top.
steps: Heat 1 1/2 tbsp olive oil in a large (12-inch) oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Add the sweet potatoes and 1/2 tsp kosher salt, cover and cook 8 minutes, stirring once or twice.
Uncover and cook 4 to 5 minutes more, stirring occasionally, until the potatoes are tender and browned at the edges. Transfer to a plate.

Add the remaining 1/2 tbsp oil, the onion and bell pepper to the skillet and cook 3 minutes. Add the turkey, smoked paprika, garlic powder, thyme, 3/4 tsp salt and 1/2 tsp pepper; cook 6 to 7 minutes, breaking it up, until no longer pink (165°F).
Return the sweet potatoes to the skillet, add the spinach and stir until wilted, about 1 minute.

Make 8 small wells in the hash and crack an egg into each. Season the eggs with salt and pepper, cover and cook over medium-low heat 5 to 7 minutes until the whites are set and the yolks are still runny (or longer to taste).
Divide into 4 portions with 2 eggs each and serve hot.

image.alt: egg on pan

title: Greek Chicken Gyro Bowls
description: Lemon-oregano chicken over rice and chickpeas with cucumber, tomatoes, red onion, feta, olives and a garlicky homemade tzatziki.
steps: Marinate the chicken: combine 1 1/2 tbsp olive oil, juice of 1 lemon, 3 cloves garlic, oregano, smoked paprika, 1 tsp kosher salt and 1/2 tsp black pepper in a bowl. Add the chicken and turn to coat; marinate at least 15 minutes (or up to 8 hours refrigerated).
Cook the rice: bring 2 cups water, the rice and 1/2 tsp salt to a boil, cover, reduce heat to low and simmer 18 minutes. Rest 5 minutes and fluff.
Make the tzatziki: squeeze the grated cucumber dry in a towel, then stir it into the Greek yogurt with the remaining garlic, dill, 1 tbsp lemon juice and a pinch of salt. Refrigerate until serving.
Heat a grill pan or large skillet over medium-high heat with the remaining 1/2 tbsp oil. Cook the chicken 6 to 7 minutes per side until 165°F inside. Rest 5 minutes, then slice thinly.
Toss the chickpeas with the remaining lemon juice and a pinch of salt.
Divide rice among 4 bowls and top with chicken, chickpeas, diced cucumber, tomatoes, red onion, feta and olives. Spoon tzatziki over the top.

image.alt: Sliced grilled chicken breast with rice and salad

title: Beef and Broccoli
description: Better-than-takeout tender flank steak and crisp broccoli in a glossy garlic-ginger soy sauce, served over jasmine rice.
steps: Cook the rice: rinse, then simmer with 1 1/2 cups water, covered, over low heat for 15 minutes; rest 5 minutes off heat.

Toss the sliced beef with 1 tbsp soy sauce and 1 tbsp cornstarch; let sit 10 minutes. In a bowl whisk the remaining soy sauce, oyster sauce, brown sugar, beef broth, sesame oil and remaining 1 tbsp cornstarch.
Heat 1 tbsp vegetable oil in a large skillet or wok over high heat. Add the broccoli and 3 tbsp water, cover and steam-fry 3 to 4 minutes until bright green and crisp-tender. Transfer to a plate.
Add the remaining 1 tbsp oil to the pan. Sear the beef in two batches, 1 to 2 minutes per side, until browned. Transfer to the plate.
Reduce heat to medium, add the garlic and ginger and stir 30 seconds. Whisk the sauce again, pour it in and simmer 1 to 2 minutes until thickened.
Return the beef and broccoli to the pan and toss to coat. Serve over rice, sprinkled with sesame seeds.

image.alt: A bowl of beef and broccoli with white rice

title: Protein Pancakes
description: Fluffy oat and Greek yogurt pancakes boosted with vanilla protein powder, topped with fresh blueberries and a drizzle of maple syrup.
steps: Blend the oats in a blender on high for 30 to 45 seconds until they form a fine flour.
Add the protein powder, Greek yogurt, eggs, milk, baking powder, cinnamon and salt. Blend 20 to 30 seconds until smooth, then let the batter rest 5 minutes to thicken.
Heat a nonstick skillet or griddle over medium-low heat (about 325°F) and brush lightly with oil.

Pour 1/4 cup batter per pancake. Cook 2 to 3 minutes until bubbles form on top and the edges look set, then flip and cook 1 to 2 minutes more. Protein batter browns quickly, so keep the heat moderate.
Repeat with remaining batter, oiling the pan as needed (makes about 16 pancakes).
Serve 4 pancakes per person topped with blueberries and 1 tbsp maple syrup each.

image.alt: a stack of pancakes covered in blueberries and syrup

title: Chicken Parmesan with Roasted Broccoli
description: Crispy Parmesan-panko chicken cutlets baked under marinara and melted mozzarella, served with garlicky lemon roasted broccoli for a lighter, protein-packed take on the classic.

ingredients.name: olive oil
ingredients.note: 3 tbsp for frying, 1 1/2 tbsp for broccoli

steps: Heat the oven to 425°F. Pound the chicken cutlets to an even 1/2-inch thickness and season with 3/4 tsp kosher salt and 1/2 tsp black pepper.
Toss the broccoli with 1 1/2 tbsp olive oil, the garlic, 1/2 tsp salt and 1/4 tsp pepper on a large sheet pan and spread in a single layer.

Set up a breading station: flour in one shallow dish, beaten eggs in a second, and panko mixed with Parmesan and Italian seasoning in a third. Dredge each cutlet in flour, dip in egg, then press firmly into the panko mixture.
Heat 3 tbsp olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Fry the cutlets 2 to 3 minutes per side until golden, working in batches if needed.

Spread 1/2 cup marinara in a baking dish, set the cutlets on top, spoon the remaining marinara over them and top with mozzarella. Bake on the upper rack, with the broccoli on the lower rack, for 15 to 18 minutes, until the cheese is bubbly, the chicken reaches 165°F and the broccoli is tender and browned at the edges.
Squeeze lemon over the broccoli. Serve each cutlet with a pile of roasted broccoli, garnished with basil and extra Parmesan.

image.alt: a plate of food with meat and broccoli

title: BBQ Chicken Stuffed Sweet Potatoes
description: Fluffy baked sweet potatoes loaded with smoky shredded BBQ chicken, melted cheddar, a cool Greek yogurt drizzle and green onions.
steps: Heat the oven to 400°F. Prick the sweet potatoes several times with a fork, set on a foil-lined sheet pan and bake 45 to 50 minutes until very tender when squeezed.

After the potatoes have baked 20 minutes, rub the chicken with olive oil, smoked paprika, garlic powder, 3/4 tsp kosher salt and 1/2 tsp black pepper. Add it to a small baking dish and bake alongside the potatoes for 20 to 25 minutes, until 165°F inside.
Shred the chicken with two forks and toss with the barbecue sauce.
Split each sweet potato lengthwise, fluff the flesh with a fork and season with a pinch of salt.
Stuff each potato with BBQ chicken, sprinkle with cheddar and return to the oven 3 to 5 minutes until the cheese melts.
Top with a spoonful of Greek yogurt, green onions and cilantro. Serve warm.

image.alt: Stuffed potato with side salad and avocado

title: Beef Chili Mac
description: A one-pot mashup of hearty beef and bean chili and cheesy elbow macaroni, with sweet corn and a blanket of melted cheddar.
steps: In a large Dutch oven or deep skillet over medium-high heat, cook the ground beef with the onion and bell pepper 7 to 8 minutes, breaking up the meat, until browned. Drain any excess fat.
Add the garlic, chili powder, cumin, smoked paprika, 1 tsp kosher salt and 1/2 tsp black pepper; stir 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in the diced tomatoes, tomato sauce, kidney beans and beef broth and bring to a boil.

Stir in the uncooked macaroni, reduce heat to medium-low, cover and simmer 12 to 14 minutes, stirring every few minutes so it doesn't stick, until the pasta is tender and most of the liquid is absorbed.
Stir in the corn and cook 2 minutes. Taste and adjust seasoning.
Sprinkle the cheddar over the top, cover and let stand off the heat 2 to 3 minutes until melted. Garnish with green onions and serve.

image.alt: A bowl of food with a spoon in it

title: Garlic Butter Shrimp Pasta
description: Juicy shrimp and spaghetti tossed in a silky garlic-butter lemon sauce with parmesan and parsley. Restaurant-worthy, on the table in 25 minutes.

ingredients.name: large shrimp
ingredients.note: peeled and deveined; thawed if frozen

steps: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Cook the spaghetti 1 minute less than the package directs (about 9 minutes). Reserve 1 cup pasta water, then drain.
While the pasta cooks, pat the shrimp dry and season with 1/2 tsp kosher salt and a few grinds of black pepper.
Heat the olive oil and 1 tbsp butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add the shrimp in a single layer and cook 1 to 2 minutes per side, just until pink. Transfer to a plate.
Reduce heat to medium. Add the remaining 3 tbsp butter, the garlic, and red pepper flakes; cook, stirring, 30 to 60 seconds until fragrant but not browned.
Pour in the chicken broth, lemon juice, and lemon zest. Simmer 2 minutes to reduce slightly.
Add the drained spaghetti, parmesan, and 1/2 cup pasta water. Toss for 1 minute until the sauce turns glossy, adding more pasta water a splash at a time if it looks dry.
Return the shrimp and any juices to the pan, toss with the parsley, and season with salt and pepper. Serve right away.

image.alt: a plate of pasta with shrimp and parsley

title: Chicken Caesar Wraps
description: Golden seared chicken, crisp romaine, parmesan, and crunchy croutons rolled up in a big tortilla with creamy Caesar dressing. A lunch that actually keeps you full.
steps: Slice the chicken breasts in half horizontally to make thin cutlets. Rub with the olive oil, garlic powder, salt, and pepper.
Heat a large skillet over medium-high heat. Cook the cutlets 4 to 5 minutes per side, until browned and the internal temperature reaches 165°F. Rest 3 minutes, then slice into strips.
In a large bowl, toss the chopped romaine with the Caesar dressing, parmesan, and crushed croutons.
Warm the tortillas in the dry skillet for about 15 seconds per side (or wrap in a damp paper towel and microwave 20 seconds) so they fold without cracking.
Divide the dressed salad and sliced chicken down the center of each tortilla. Fold in the sides, roll up tightly, and cut in half on the diagonal.

image.alt: A wrap and salad on a white plate

title: Chicken and Black Bean Quesadillas
description: Crispy, cheesy quesadillas stuffed with rotisserie chicken, smoky black beans, and salsa. A weeknight crowd-pleaser kids love.
steps: In a bowl, mix the shredded chicken, black beans, salsa, cumin, and chili powder. Lightly mash about a quarter of the beans with a fork so the filling holds together.
Lay out 4 tortillas. Sprinkle each with 3 tbsp cheese, spread a quarter of the chicken mixture on top, add the green onions, then another 3 tbsp cheese. Top with the remaining tortillas.
Heat a large skillet or griddle over medium heat and coat lightly with cooking spray.

Cook one or two quesadillas at a time for 2 to 3 minutes per side, pressing gently with a spatula, until golden and crisp and the cheese is melted. Keep finished ones warm on a sheet pan in a 200°F oven.
Rest 1 minute, cut each into wedges, and serve with sour cream and extra salsa.

image.alt: a plate topped with a quesadilla cut in half

title: Pesto Gnocchi with Cherry Tomatoes
description: Pan-crisped potato gnocchi tossed with basil pesto, blistered cherry tomatoes, and wilted spinach. One skillet, 20 minutes, zero boiling.
steps: Heat 1 tbsp olive oil in a large nonstick skillet over medium-high heat. Add the gnocchi straight from the package in a single layer and cook undisturbed for 3 minutes, until golden on the bottom.
Stir and continue cooking 3 to 4 minutes more, until golden all over and tender inside. Transfer to a bowl.
Add the remaining 1 tbsp olive oil and the cherry tomatoes to the skillet. Cook 4 to 5 minutes, shaking the pan, until the tomatoes blister and some burst. Add the garlic and cook 30 seconds.
Add the spinach and stir until just wilted, about 1 minute.
Return the gnocchi to the pan, remove from the heat, and toss with the pesto and 2 tbsp water to loosen it into a sauce.
Season with salt and pepper, top with parmesan, and serve hot.

image.alt: black ceramic plate with food

title: Korean Ground Beef Bowls
description: Sweet-savory ground beef glazed with soy, garlic, ginger, and sesame over fluffy rice with crunchy cucumber and carrots. Bulgogi flavor for a fraction of the effort.
steps: Rinse the rice and cook with 2 1/4 cups water: bring to a boil, cover, reduce heat to low, and simmer 15 minutes. Remove from heat and let steam, covered, 5 minutes.
Meanwhile, whisk the soy sauce, brown sugar, sesame oil, and red pepper flakes in a small bowl.
Heat a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add the ground beef and cook 5 to 6 minutes, breaking it up, until browned and no longer pink. Drain any excess fat.
Push the beef to the side, add the garlic and ginger to the open space, and cook 30 seconds until fragrant. Stir into the beef.
Pour in the sauce and simmer 2 to 3 minutes, stirring, until it reduces and glazes the beef.
Divide the rice among bowls, top with the beef, cucumber, and carrots, and finish with green onions and sesame seeds.

image.alt: a plate of rice, cucumbers, and meat on a table

title: Caprese Chicken
description: Seared Italian-seasoned chicken cutlets topped with melty fresh mozzarella, juicy tomatoes, basil, and a drizzle of balsamic glaze. High protein, low effort.
steps: Heat the broiler to high with a rack about 6 inches from the element.
Slice each chicken breast in half horizontally to make 4 even cutlets about 1/2 inch thick. Season both sides with Italian seasoning, garlic powder, salt, and pepper.
Heat the olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Sear the cutlets 4 to 5 minutes per side until golden and the internal temperature reaches 165°F.
Top each cutlet with tomato slices and mozzarella slices.
Slide the skillet under the broiler for 2 to 3 minutes, watching closely, until the cheese is melted and lightly browned.
Scatter the basil over the top, drizzle with balsamic glaze, and serve.

image.alt: Chicken with tomatoes and basil
image.photographer: Rodrigo Rodrigues | WOLF Λ R T

title: Sesame Peanut Noodles
description: Slurpable noodles coated in a creamy peanut-sesame sauce and tossed with crunchy cucumber, carrots, and bell pepper. Great warm or cold, and even better for lunch the next day.
steps: Bring a large pot of water to a boil and cook the noodles according to package directions (8 to 10 minutes). Reserve 1/2 cup cooking water, drain, and rinse briefly under cool water if serving cold.
While the noodles cook, whisk the peanut butter, soy sauce, rice vinegar, honey, sesame oil, sriracha, garlic, and ginger in a large bowl until smooth.
Whisk in 3 to 4 tbsp of hot water (or reserved pasta water) until the sauce is pourable, like heavy cream.
Prep the cucumber, carrots, bell pepper, green onions, and cilantro.
Add the noodles to the sauce and toss until evenly coated, loosening with more reserved water if needed.
Toss in the vegetables, then top with chopped peanuts, sesame seeds, and cilantro. Serve warm, at room temperature, or chilled.

image.alt: white ceramic bowl with noodles and chopsticks

title: Shakshuka
description: Eggs gently poached in a smoky, spiced tomato and pepper sauce, finished with feta and herbs. Bring the skillet to the table with crusty bread for dipping.
steps: Heat the olive oil in a 12-inch skillet over medium heat. Add the onion and bell pepper with a pinch of salt and cook 6 to 7 minutes, stirring, until soft.
Add the garlic, smoked paprika, cumin, and red pepper flakes and cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in the crushed tomatoes, season with 1/2 tsp salt and some pepper, and simmer 5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until slightly thickened.
Use a spoon to make 8 wells in the sauce and crack an egg into each.
Cover the skillet and cook over medium-low heat 6 to 8 minutes, until the whites are set but the yolks are still runny.
Sprinkle with feta and parsley. Toast the bread and serve it alongside for dipping.

image.alt: a skillet with eggs and tomatoes on a table

title: Avocado Toast with Fried Egg
description: Crisp whole-grain toast piled with lemony smashed avocado and a jammy fried egg, finished with chili flakes. A 10-minute breakfast with staying power.
steps: Toast the bread until deeply golden and crisp.
Halve and pit the avocados, scoop into a bowl, and mash with the lemon juice and 1/4 tsp kosher salt until mostly smooth with a few chunks.

Melt the butter in a large nonstick skillet over medium heat. Crack in the eggs and cook 2 to 3 minutes, until the whites are set and edges are lightly crisp. Cover for the last 30 seconds if you like the tops more set.
Spread the avocado evenly over the toast.
Top each slice with a fried egg, then finish with black pepper, red pepper flakes, and a pinch of salt. Serve immediately.

image.alt: Avocado toast with two fried eggs and microgreens

title: Tomato Basil Soup with Grilled Cheese
description: A velvety, lightly creamy tomato basil soup paired with buttery, golden cheddar grilled cheese for dunking. Pure comfort in 30 minutes.

ingredients.name: unsalted butter
ingredients.note: 2 tbsp for soup, 3 tbsp softened for sandwiches

steps: Melt 2 tbsp butter in a medium pot over medium heat. Add the onion and cook 5 minutes until soft, then add the garlic and cook 30 seconds.
Stir in the crushed tomatoes, vegetable broth, sugar, 1/2 tsp salt, and a few grinds of pepper. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer 10 minutes.
Meanwhile, spread the softened 3 tbsp butter on one side of each bread slice. Build 4 sandwiches with the cheddar inside and the buttered sides facing out.
Cook the sandwiches in a large skillet over medium-low heat 3 to 4 minutes per side, until deep golden and the cheese is melted.
Remove the soup from the heat, add the basil, and blend until smooth with an immersion blender (or carefully in a blender, venting the lid). Stir in the heavy cream and adjust salt and pepper.
Cut the grilled cheese into halves or strips and serve with bowls of soup garnished with basil.

image.alt: Tomato soup with grilled cheese sandwich

title: Classic Spaghetti and Meatballs
description: Tender, parmesan-flecked beef meatballs simmered in marinara and piled over spaghetti. The Sunday-dinner classic, made doable on a weeknight.
steps: In a large bowl, stir together the breadcrumbs, 1/4 cup parmesan, egg, milk, garlic, salt and pepper. Add the ground beef and mix gently with your hands until just combined; overmixing makes tough meatballs.
Roll into 16 meatballs about 1 1/2 inches wide (a great job for kids with clean hands).
Heat the olive oil in a large deep skillet or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Brown the meatballs in a single layer, turning, for 6-8 minutes until browned on most sides.
Pour the marinara over the meatballs, bring to a gentle simmer, cover and cook over medium-low heat for 15-18 minutes, until the meatballs reach 160°F inside.
Meanwhile, bring a large pot of well-salted water to a boil and cook the spaghetti according to package directions until al dente. Reserve 1/2 cup pasta water, then drain.
Toss the spaghetti with a few spoonfuls of sauce, loosening with pasta water if needed. Serve topped with meatballs, more sauce, the remaining parmesan and torn basil.

image.alt: a white plate topped with spaghetti and meatballs

title: Stovetop Mac and Cheese
description: Ultra-creamy, from-scratch mac and cheese made in one pot with sharp cheddar. Ready faster than the boxed kind takes to boil, and miles better.

ingredients.name: shredded sharp cheddar cheese
ingredients.note: about 2 cups; shred from a block for the smoothest sauce

steps: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Cook the macaroni 1 minute less than the package directions (about 6-7 minutes), then drain and set aside.
Return the pot to medium heat and melt the butter. Whisk in the flour and cook, whisking, for 1 minute until bubbly and lightly golden.
Slowly whisk in the warm milk, a splash at a time, until smooth. Simmer, whisking often, for 4-5 minutes until the sauce coats the back of a spoon.
Remove the pot from the heat. Stir in the cheddar a handful at a time until melted, then season with garlic powder, mustard powder, salt and pepper.
Add the drained macaroni and stir over low heat for 1-2 minutes until hot and creamy. Splash in a little more milk if it thickens. Serve right away.

image.alt: a bowl of macaroni and cheese

title: Baked Chicken Tenders with Honey Mustard
description: Golden, crunchy parmesan-panko chicken tenders baked instead of fried, with a three-ingredient honey mustard for dunking.

ingredients.name: chicken tenderloins
ingredients.note: or boneless skinless chicken breasts cut into strips

steps: Heat the oven to 425°F. Line a rimmed sheet pan with foil and set a wire rack on top; mist the rack with cooking spray.
Set up three shallow dishes: flour mixed with 1/2 tsp salt; eggs beaten with 1 tbsp water; and panko mixed with parmesan, garlic powder, paprika, the remaining salt and the pepper.
Pat the chicken dry. Dredge each tender in flour, dip in egg, then press firmly into the panko mixture to coat all sides. Arrange on the rack without touching.
Spray the tops generously with cooking spray. Bake 16-18 minutes, until golden and crisp and the thickest piece reaches 165°F.
While the chicken bakes, whisk together the mayonnaise, Dijon and honey in a small bowl.
Let the tenders rest 2 minutes, then serve with the honey mustard for dipping.

image.alt: fried chicken on white ceramic plate

title: Homemade Pepperoni Pizza
description: Two classic round pepperoni pizzas with crisp, golden crusts, made with store-bought dough and baked on a hot pan or pizza stone. Cheaper and faster than delivery.

ingredients.name: refrigerated pizza dough
ingredients.note: store-bought, enough for two 12-inch pizzas; at room temperature 30 minutes

ingredients.name: olive oil
ingredients.note: divided, for the pans and crust

steps: Place a pizza stone or two pizza pans on the lowest oven rack and heat the oven to 500°F for at least 30 minutes (a stone needs the full time to get hot). If using pans without a stone, heat the oven 15 minutes.

Divide the dough into 2 equal pieces. On a lightly floured counter, press and stretch each into a 12-inch round, leaving the edge slightly thicker. If it springs back, let it rest 5 minutes and try again.

For a stone, set a round on a floured pizza peel or the back of a sheet pan; for pans, brush each pan with 1/2 tbsp olive oil and lay a round in it. Brush the rims of the dough with the remaining olive oil.
Spread 1/2 cup pizza sauce over each round, leaving a 1/2-inch border. Top each with half the mozzarella, then the pepperoni, and sprinkle with Italian seasoning.

Slide the pizza onto the hot stone (or put the pan on the lowest rack) and bake 10-13 minutes, until the crust is deep golden and the cheese is bubbling and browned in spots. Repeat with the second pizza if baking one at a time.
Cool 3-5 minutes, sprinkle with parmesan, and cut each pizza into 8 slices.

image.alt: a pepperoni pizza sitting on top of a wooden cutting board

title: Ground Beef Tacos
description: Taco night done right: juicy beef seasoned with a homemade spice blend, tucked into crunchy shells with all the fixings. Everyone builds their own.
steps: Heat the oven to 350°F for the taco shells. Stir together the chili powder, cumin, garlic powder, onion powder, paprika, oregano and salt in a small bowl.
Cook the ground beef in a large skillet over medium-high heat, breaking it up, for 6-7 minutes until no pink remains. Drain off excess fat.
Stir in the spice mix and tomato paste and cook 1 minute until fragrant. Add the water and simmer 4-5 minutes, stirring, until saucy and thick.
Meanwhile, stand the taco shells on a sheet pan and warm in the oven for 5-6 minutes until crisp.
Set out the lettuce, tomatoes, cheddar, sour cream and salsa. Spoon the beef into shells and let everyone top their own.

title: Chicken Pot Pie
description: A creamy chicken and vegetable filling under a flaky golden crust. A rotisserie chicken and store-bought pie crust make this cozy classic weeknight-friendly.
steps: Heat the oven to 400°F. Let the pie crust sit at room temperature while you make the filling.
Melt the butter in a large oven-safe skillet (10-inch) over medium heat. Add the onion, carrots and celery and cook 6-8 minutes until softened. Add the garlic and cook 30 seconds.
Sprinkle in the flour and stir for 1 minute. Slowly stir in the broth, then the milk, and simmer 3-4 minutes until thick and creamy.
Stir in the chicken, peas, thyme, salt and pepper. Remove from the heat. (If you don't have an oven-safe skillet, transfer the filling to a 9-inch deep-dish pie plate.)
Lay the pie crust over the filling, tuck or crimp the edges, brush with beaten egg and cut 4 small slits in the top for steam.
Set the skillet on a sheet pan and bake 25-30 minutes, until the crust is deep golden and the filling bubbles at the edges. Rest 10 minutes before serving.

title: Cheeseburger Sliders
description: A whole tray of melty cheeseburger sliders on sweet Hawaiian rolls, baked all at once with a garlic-butter top. Party food that doubles as an easy dinner.
steps: Heat the oven to 400°F. In a 9x13-inch baking dish, mix the ground beef, onion, salt and pepper, then press it into an even layer covering the bottom of the dish.
Bake the beef 15 minutes, until cooked through (160°F). Lift the beef slab onto a cutting board with two spatulas and pour off the fat; wipe out the dish.
Without separating the rolls, slice the whole slab in half horizontally. Place the bottom half in the baking dish.
Layer on 3 cheese slices, the beef slab, the remaining 3 cheese slices and the pickles. Squeeze ketchup and mustard over the top, then add the top half of the rolls.
Stir the melted butter with the garlic powder, brush over the rolls and sprinkle with sesame seeds.
Cover with foil and bake 5 minutes, then uncover and bake 4-5 minutes more until the tops are golden and the cheese is melted. Cut into 12 sliders (3 per person).

title: Homemade Chicken Noodle Soup
description: Comforting, golden chicken noodle soup with tender chicken, carrots, celery and egg noodles in a thyme-scented broth. Ready in under an hour.
steps: Heat the olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium heat. Add the onion, carrots and celery and cook 6-7 minutes until softened. Add the garlic and cook 30 seconds.

Add the broth, thyme, bay leaf, salt and pepper and bring to a boil. Nestle in the whole chicken breasts, reduce to a gentle simmer, cover partially and cook 15-18 minutes until the chicken reaches 165°F.
Transfer the chicken to a cutting board and shred with two forks.
Return the soup to a boil, add the egg noodles and cook 6-8 minutes until tender.
Stir the shredded chicken back in, remove the bay leaf, and add the parsley and a squeeze of lemon. Taste and adjust salt before serving.
For leftovers or freezing, store the noodles separately so they don't soak up all the broth.

title: French Toast Bake
description: All the cinnamon-vanilla goodness of French toast baked in one dish with a crackly brown-sugar top, finished with juicy orange segments and toasted pecans. Assemble the night before for an easy weekend breakfast.

ingredients.name: French bread
ingredients.note: 1 loaf, cut into 1-inch cubes (day-old is best)

ingredients.name: unsalted butter
ingredients.note: melted, plus more for the dish

steps: Butter a 9x13-inch baking dish and spread the bread cubes in it.
Whisk the eggs, milk, 1/3 cup brown sugar, vanilla, cinnamon and salt until smooth. Pour evenly over the bread and press gently so every piece soaks.
Cover and let soak at least 20 minutes at room temperature, or refrigerate overnight (up to 12 hours).

Heat the oven to 350°F. Stir the melted butter with the remaining 2 tbsp brown sugar and drizzle over the top. Toast the pecans on a small sheet pan in the oven for 6-8 minutes while it heats, then set aside.
Bake uncovered 40-45 minutes, until puffed, golden and set in the center (a knife should come out without wet egg). Tent with foil if the top browns too fast.
Rest 5 minutes, then scatter the orange segments and toasted pecans over the top and serve warm with maple syrup.

title: Slow Cooker BBQ Pulled Pork Sandwiches
description: Fall-apart tender pork shoulder rubbed with smoky spices, slow cooked in tangy BBQ sauce and piled onto soft buns with crunchy coleslaw.

ingredients.name: boneless pork shoulder
ingredients.note: also sold as pork butt; trimmed of excess fat

steps: Mix the brown sugar, smoked paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, salt and pepper and rub it all over the pork.
Scatter the sliced onion in the bottom of a 6-quart slow cooker. Set the pork on top, then pour 1 cup barbecue sauce and the vinegar over it.
Cover and cook on LOW for 8-9 hours (or HIGH for 5-6 hours), until the pork shreds easily with a fork.
Transfer the pork to a cutting board and shred with two forks, discarding any large pieces of fat. Skim the fat from the cooking liquid.
Return the pork to the slow cooker and toss with the remaining 1/2 cup barbecue sauce plus enough cooking liquid to keep it juicy.
Toss the coleslaw mix with the dressing. Toast the buns if you like, then pile on the pork and top with slaw. Leftover pork freezes well for up to 3 months.
